scope: Explicit combined deployment reconnect from saved transaction identifier
behavior: Historical deployment bytes, seven saved policy fields and eight SDK-exposed release verifier keys must match before offering address review.
Reconnect verifies exact joined address and current program, derived vendor owner key, policy digests and windows.
A new encrypted v7 browser copy retaining the identifier is written before opening the session; the original copy is preserved.
Three-minute continuation deadline and unmount checks prevent late reads from installing a session. Already-started storage may commit late.
Combined checkpoint and recovery v7 accept canonical lowercase 64- or 66-character hex transaction identifiers. Other 32-byte bindings are unchanged.

reproduction.command: CI=1 npx playwright test e2e/combined-deployment-recovery.spec.ts e2e/deployment-policy.spec.ts
reproduction.cause: Captured Preprod transaction uses 66-character identifiers; v7 initially reused the 64-character key/commitment validator. Both desktop and mobile failed before restoration. The deployment checkpoint had the same restriction and was corrected too.

unit.command: npm run test:run -w @vulnseal/web -- src/App.deployment-checkpoint.test.tsx src/App.network.test.tsx src/DeploymentPolicyCheck.test.tsx src/recovery.test.ts
coverage: Success with decrypted saved-copy equality and no second deployment
Owner/policy/address mismatch; failed storage; late ledger read after timeout/unmount
Policy/key mismatch, missing/unexpected/duplicate/absent verifier comparison prevents address selection
64- and 66-character recovery round trips; malformed lengths rejected; checkpoint suite uses 66-character identifier

limitations: Successful wallet/SDK reconnect is mocked in application tests. Browser checks use captured network evidence and actual worker, with mismatching local intent.
No native wallet signing, authenticated inclusion or proof/signature verification, physical suspend test, full regression or container refresh.
Verifier comparison does not establish source-to-key generation or exclude other key versions.
Combined report submissions/transitions still lack mandatory durable identifier journals.
